Link
Ethereum L1 and Base ended their joint effort to unify account-abstraction and wallet standards. Ethereum is prioritizing censorship resistance and privacy, and Base is prioritizing compliance and scalability.
Wallet interoperability across L2s gets messier in the near term. Ethereum's core roadmap and its largest L2 by activity are pulling in different directions.

Base introduces transactions that can wait
Base is adding Validity Transactions in its upcoming Cobalt upgrade. A transaction can be signed in advance with a set of conditions, and Base will only include it in a block once all conditions are met.
The first version supports simple conditions such as an address balance, a contract value, or a block number. This means things like limit orders, mints, TGE, claims, unlocks, liquidations, and AI agent payments could work without bots constantly monitoring the network and competing to submit transactions.
One transaction can also trigger another. If the first transaction changes a required contract value, the second one becomes valid immediately and can potentially be included in the same block.
The feature is still limited: transactions wait for around a minute, conditions are visible to Base nodes, and there is no direct way to check things like token prices. Developers also recommend keeping final checks inside the smart contract to prevent MEV issues.
